text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- The tripartite agreement between the State Oil Company of the Azerbaijani Republic (SOCAR), the Russian Ministry of Fuel and Energy and the Southern Oil Company (YUNKO) of the Chechen Republic on the transportation of Azerbaijani oil from Baku to Novorossiisk via Grozny, signed in Baku on Friday evening, does not regard Chechnya as an independent state.
- President Yeltsin's radio address appeal to bring in a new generation of company managers to match Russia's young cabinet may push some older directors towards his opponents.
- Russia is not likely to walk out of the game and is already "spinning its geopolitical web", says the paper commenting on the results of the NATO summit in Madrid.

- Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who heads a government commission on nuclear weapons, was shown new designs for atomic weapons while visiting the Arzamaz 16 research centre about 400 km (250 miles) southeast of Moscow.

- A conference of doctors concluded on Friday that Russia's top military commander Anatoly Romanov, who had been in a coma since being caught a bomb blast in Chechnya in October 1995, is making slow progress.
SEVODNYA

- A story, spread on Friday by Russian mass media about prosecutors investigating an alleged corruption case involving former top-ranking officials and certain commercial banks, may grow into a major financial and political sensation. The scandal surrounding former justice minister Valentin Kovalyev looks like a child's play by comparison, says the paper.
- The central bank of Russia doubled the minimum charter capital for foreign bank subsidiaries in Russia in the next three months.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIYA

- The paper denounces a sudden swoop by NATO forces on Bosnian Serb war crimes suspects as the beginning of a manhunt and warns NATO leaders against forgetting the historic precedents in former Yugoslavia, which led to several serious conflicts in Europe.
IZVESTIA
- Russia is unlikely to protest too strongly against the incident involving NATO commandos in Bosnia in the run-up to the Russian-U.S. foreign ministers' meeting in St Petersburg.
- Russian neo-Nazis are honing their combat skills and awaiting the signal to install "Russian order".
- Russian and Ukrainian special services have arrested a woman suspected of setting off a bomb at a railway station in the south of Russia last April.
- Russian prosecutors are investigating an alleged corruption case involving former top-ranking officials and certain commercial banks.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- NATO countries are in no hurry to finance modernisation of the armies of new alliance members.
- Russian pensioners who have received all pension arrears in July are nervously wondering whether they will have to wait for future installments.
- Foreign ministers from leading European countries are coming to Russia over the next week.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- British-registered Trans World Group may compete with Russian UNEXIMbank for control of the giant Norilsk Nikel smelter.
-- Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
